turns.content: A 10 lb weight stretches a spring for 2 seconds. Determine the spring constant in consistent force-length units.
Let u(t) be displacement from equilibrium. Using g=32 ft/s, convert the weight to mass in slugs and write the equation of motion and angular frequency.
Solve that differential equation for the general function u(t).
The mass starts 2 in below equilibrium with an upward velocity of 1 ft. Apply these initial conditions to determine the two constants.
Use the coefficients to compute the amplitude in seconds, with the equivalent inches if convenient.
Check the sign of the initial derivative, the units of the coefficients, and whether the reported extremal magnitude is consistent with the supplied initial data.
Report the resulting function u(t) and its characteristic magnitude with suitable numerical precision.
